title: Regular base change preserves regular alteration pairs
statement:
Let $g:S'\to S$ be a regular morphism of Noetherian schemes, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres, and let $\ell$ be prime invertible on $S$. Suppose $S,S'$ are reduced and $(q_i:R_i\to S)_i$ is a finite covering family in the topology of $\ell'$-alterations, with every $R_i$ regular Noetherian. Suppose the usual fibre products $R'_i=R_i\times_S S'$ are Noetherian (in particular this holds when $S'$ is Noetherian and the $q_i$ are finite type). Then the $R'_i$ are regular, are objects of $\operatorname{alt}/S'$, and form a covering family. If a nowhere dense closed subset $Z\subset S$ has inverse image on each $R_i$ equal to the support of a strict normal crossings boundary, the same assertion holds for $g^{-1}Z$ on each $R'_i$, allowing the empty boundary. Regular means regular local rings at all points; geometrically regular means regular after all finite residue-field extensions. A complete local ring of a local excellent Noetherian scheme is regular over that local scheme, and hence over the original scheme when formed by localization followed by completion.

Conventions for the notions used here: [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].
